source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for prefill. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Prefill processes the prompt and is generally parallel across prompt tokens; its cost is dominated by prompt processing and often compute utilization.
corrected_answer: Assume a fixed model revision, tokenizer, precision, runtime, hardware, and causal attention. Compare a prefill run against a matched implementation while sweeping prompt-token count and batch size; the concrete mechanism is that prefill applies the transformer to all prompt positions and materializes each layer's K/V state, which subsequent decode steps read rather than recompute. Record prompt tokens/s, prefill latency, peak device memory, kernel utilization, and resulting decode inter-token latency, with warm-up and repeated trials. Boundary condition: the K/V state is reusable only for an exactly compatible prefix and the same model/positional settings; a changed prefix or cache eviction forces work again. Interpret differences only with identical tokenization, concurrency, memory accounting, and cache policy; report medians and tail latency rather than attributing every change to prefill compute.
risks: Prefill and decode behavior depends on runtime kernels, precision, batching, prompt lengths, and cache policy.
Non-equivalent baselines or cache hits can confound attribution of latency and memory changes.
evidence_required: Profiler traces separating prefill and decode, including kernel time, memory transfers, and cache allocation.
Repeated matched sweeps over prompt length, batch or concurrency, precision, and cache state with median and tail latency.

source_user: Write a concise runbook entry for an engineer investigating prefill. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Prefill processes the prompt and is generally parallel across prompt tokens; its cost is dominated by prompt processing and often compute utilization.
corrected_answer: Runbook: first pin model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, runtime, prompt length, and concurrency. Capture separate prefill latency, prompt tokens/s, peak memory, GPU utilization, cache bytes, and decode inter-token latency after warm-up; repeat enough trials to report median and p95. Mechanism: prefill performs the prompt's parallel transformer forward pass and writes per-layer K/V entries that decode reads on later steps. If prefill is unexpectedly slow, check token count, padding/packing, kernel selection, host-to-device transfers, batching, and cache allocation before changing the model. Boundary condition: a cache helps only when the later request has an exactly matching compatible prefix and enough capacity; prefix changes, eviction, unsupported positional settings, or recomputation invalidate that assumption. Do not compare unlike precision, batch, context, or cache states.
risks: Prefill and decode behavior depends on runtime kernels, precision, batching, prompt lengths, and cache policy.
Non-equivalent baselines or cache hits can confound attribution of latency and memory changes.
evidence_required: Profiler traces separating prefill and decode, including kernel time, memory transfers, and cache allocation.
Repeated matched sweeps over prompt length, batch or concurrency, precision, and cache state with median and tail latency.

source_user: Define decode and explain one reason it matters in LLM infrastructure. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Decode is the autoregressive phase after prompt prefill: at each step the model produces the next token and appends its new key/value vectors to the per-layer KV cache. It matters because a serving system repeatedly reads model weights and the growing cache for a small amount of new-token computation, so memory bandwidth, cache capacity, and scheduler batching can determine inter-token latency. Boundary condition: this is not a universal bottleneck—short prompts, large batches, kernels, quantization, and hardware can shift the limiting resource. Measure tokens/s, median and p95 inter-token latency, peak memory, cache occupancy, batch/concurrency, and utilization under a fixed model, precision, context length, and sampling setup; separate prefill latency from decode latency and do not infer serving behavior from training throughput.
risks: Prefill and decode behavior depends on runtime kernels, precision, batching, prompt lengths, and cache policy.
Non-equivalent baselines or cache hits can confound attribution of latency and memory changes.
evidence_required: Profiler traces separating prefill and decode, including kernel time, memory transfers, and cache allocation.
Repeated matched sweeps over prompt length, batch or concurrency, precision, and cache state with median and tail latency.
